persons.note: THE 1835 POLL LIST ALONE. Read from poll_1835. THE GRADE IS THE OWNER'S RATIFIED LADDER OF 2026-09-03 (G2a), applied to every identity at once by tools/consolidate_resident_evidence.py and spent onto this card by tools/mint_civic_residents.py; the evidence blocks below carry the reading AS READ, its locator and the record it came from, so the page can be gone back to. WHAT IS RECONSTRUCTED: everything except the person and the sources — no dwelling, no trade, no origin, no family, no party. A BOUND FROM THE RECORD, NOT AN ARRIVAL. poll_1835 names this person at Chicago by 31 December 1835 and nothing says when they came. THE BOUND FALLS AFTER THE SCENE DATE and the record says so rather than narrowing it: the earliest source that names this person is later than 1 July 1835, so they may have arrived after the day this scene models. present_on_scene_date is `uncertain` for that reason. No figure is drawn (L1). THE TOWN'S OWN ROLLS, 1833-1835 — CORROBORATION, NOT A GRADE. The early Chicago voter and tax lists held by the Illinois Regional Archives Depository name this person 1 time: Poll list of 1835 — “Bread, A.O.T.” (poll_1835_009, line 294). These are the town's own contemporary paper rather than a recollection of it, and each appearance says that a man of that name stood on that roll in that year — no more. The reading is twice mediated (Schulz's transcription, then Genealogy Trails' republication) and this project has not seen the IRAD originals. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) the 1835 poll with a second independent source is attested, the 1835 poll alone or a 1833/1834 list with another source is inferred, and a single appearance with nothing else is a projected resident. This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE — T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: one resident of the surname 'Bread' agrees with the entry's forenames; 1 bearer(s) of the surname were considered. (data/research/civic/voter_crosswalk.json).

persons.name: Albert F. Dow
persons.note: PROJECTED RESIDENT. Documented in Chicago post-office evidence but not independently corroborated strongly enough for attested circa-1835 residence. KNOWN ONLY FROM THE POST OFFICE, IN ONE RETURN. The papers print 'Dow, Albert F.' in a single return of letters uncalled-for at the Chicago post office — the Democrat of 1 July 1835, column 4 — dated 1835-07-01. Nothing else in the corpus names this person: no trade, no street, no household, no arrival, so every other claim here is written unattested in its own block. WHAT THAT IS WORTH: a correspondent believed a person of this name reachable at Chicago on that date, and nothing further — not that they lived here, kept a trade here, or were here on 1 July 1835. It is the weakest evidence this project accepts for a resident, and a source placing them elsewhere retires the record. persons.name: Sabrina A. Mason
persons.note: PROJECTED RESIDENT. Documented in Chicago post-office evidence but not independently corroborated strongly enough for attested circa-1835 residence. KNOWN ONLY FROM THE POST OFFICE, IN ONE RETURN. The papers print 'Mason Sabrina A.' in a single return of letters uncalled-for at the Chicago post office — the Democrat of 1 July 1835, column 5 — dated 1835-07-01. Nothing else in the corpus names this person: no trade, no street, no household, no arrival, so every other claim here is written unattested in its own block. WHAT THAT IS WORTH: a correspondent believed a person of this name reachable at Chicago on that date, and nothing further — not that they lived here, kept a trade here, or were here on 1 July 1835. It is the weakest evidence this project accepts for a resident, and a source placing them elsewhere retires the record. THE ARGUMENT EVERY RECORD OF THIS KIND SHARES is written once instead of once per file: the ruling of 2026-08-30 and what it cost the town (docs/LIBERTIES.md L214), the refusals and the transcription standard behind the reading (tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py). No figure is drawn (L1).

residents.research_note: MINTED FROM THE LETTER LISTS (T-0378, T-0379). citations.citation: Chicago · July 1835: Building Inventory and Architectural Reconstruction Specification. Prepared for Kevin Haas, August 2026.
what_it_supplies: A 665-roof production target with independently reconcilable group, district, level, and construction totals.
Thirty-five architectural family definitions with dimensional and massing bands.
District character, spacing, variation, finish, and chronology constraints for a July 1835 reconstruction.
A required distinction between named documentary landmarks and anonymous inferred infill.
what_it_does_not_supply: A surviving July 1835 building census or parcel-by-parcel roof register.
Exact locations, dimensions, appearance, occupants, or construction dates for anonymous roofs.
Authority to replace stronger building-specific evidence already represented in the dataset.

research_note: RECONSTRUCTED / GENERATED, NOT AN ATTESTED NAMED BUILDING. Aggregate mix follows the supplied specification; exact presence, position, footprint, finish and instance-level form are interpretive. H2 boarding-house massing currently uses a generic rectangular frame block because no boarding-house generator is implemented.

fabric_basis.words: ochre-washed clapboard on a balloon frame under a new roof — a merchant's or professional house, new-built (rule F-M: a merchant's or professional man's by its type)

sizes.upper_windows: ceil(20 crowded beds / 3 to a chamber) = 7, held to 5-10 (the house's own five bays to the H3 crosswalk's top) = 7: 7 across the upper storey of the front and of the rear
sizes.stovepipes: ceil(9 ordinary beds / 3 to a stove) = 3, held to 2-6: 3
sizes.chimneys: not sized by the beds: the two brick stacks are the household's kitchen and common-room hearths, and the stoves the beds add go out through the roof as stovepipes

lodging.note: The town model puts a boarding house at 9 people on an ordinary night and 21 when full, from the 1840 household tail (p90 and p99 of 964 Chicago households). This building takes the share of its class's total that its 198 m² of enclosed floor (99 m² × 2 storeys) is of the class's floor area.
lodging.replaceable_by: Any source that states this house's rooms, beds or lodgers on a dated day: an advertisement counting its rooms, a traveller's account of how many it slept, a licence return. A stated capacity retires the apportioned one outright.

occupancy.statement: 9 on this card against an ordinary night's 9 beds: 1 seated here from elsewhere in the layer, where no source gives them a roof, 7 drawn against the order book's lodging buckets for beds that were standing empty, a keeper drawn for a roof this programme raised.
occupancy.keeper_owed: Minted by this stage as the keeper. T-1533 drew this keeper's own children here — 2 of them — out of the book's `under_10` lodging cells, at the size the 1840 histogram gives the household. What is still owed is a SPOUSE, which no rule this project has made can draw for a keeper who is a woman; the ledger's `keeper_families` row states it, and the staffing under a keeper is T-1183's.
